text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"cat > /tmp/exposed-shortcut-design-astra.md <<'EOF'
Keep the shortcut in SearchPage.svelte. Its existing svelte:window listener already has the right lifetime, and bind:this already supplies the search input. A reusable action would add a second listener, cleanup, and a callback contract for a single caller.

Represent the platform choice as a local named union, type SearchShortcutModifier = "meta" | "control". Resolve it once from navigator.platform at component initialization, treating Mac platforms as meta and all others as control. This application already reads window during initialization, so this introduces no new rendering constraint. Derive both the visible label, "⌘ K" or "Ctrl K", and the event predicate from this one value. Keep the hint in the existing empty-query kbd slot. A const table indexed by the modifier can also supply labels and exact modifier booleans without two platform checks.

At the top of shortcut, return for event.isComposing or the existing composing state. For the new command, require event.key.toLowerCase() === "k", no altKey or shiftKey, and exactly the chosen modifier: metaKey && !ctrlKey on Mac, ctrlKey && !metaKey elsewhere. On a match, preventDefault(), input.focus(), and return. Apply this before the editing-target check so the command also works from the threshold slider or an editable control. Focus only. Do not select, clear, submit, or rewrite the URL. Repeating the command remains harmless.

Keep slash's existing editing exclusion and modifier checks. Its existing behavior allows a Shift-produced slash, which matters on some keyboard layouts. Keep Escape scoped to target === input and clearSearch(), with the composition guard preventing an IME cancellation from clearing the query. Respect event.defaultPrevented at entry if the page's other controls consume key events.

Extend browser verification with platform cases installed through page.addInitScript before navigation. Each case asserts its visible hint and uses page.keyboard.press for its expected chord. Start with a populated query and focus the threshold slider, then assert search focus, unchanged input value, unchanged URL, and no extra search request. Also invoke the chord while the search input already has focus. Test the other platform's modifier and extra modifiers with cancelable dispatched key events to avoid browser chrome shortcuts, checking neither focus transfer nor preventDefault. Dispatch composing keydown and a compositionstart/keydown/compositionend sequence to exercise both IME guards. Retain the existing slash and Escape browser test. Finally navigate to a real detail route and show the same cancelable keydown is no longer prevented, proving listener disposal. Capture a desktop screenshot with the empty search field so the new hint can be inspected for clipping.
EOF","max_output_tokens":1000}));

content.text:
Wrote design to [/tmp/exposed-shortcut-design-astra.md](/tmp/exposed-shortcut-design-astra.md).

Recommend the existing component listener, one named modifier choice shared by matching and hint, exact modifiers, composition guards, and focus without query mutation. Browser checks cover both platforms, modifier rejection, IME, preservation, and listener disposal.
